angle: Agents don’t fail on intelligence; they fail on work design, guardrails, and ownership.
sourceTitle: Stacking the odds: A blueprint for successfully scaling agentic AI
linkedinPost:
Agentic AI is racing ahead. The work it’s meant to do is not.

McKinsey outlines a blueprint for scaling agents, and the key theme resonates: companies deploy agents faster than they redesign the jobs, controls, and metrics around them.

What works in production: treat agents like employees with badges. Give each a clear job description (inputs, outputs, success criteria), a supervisor (human or system), and SLOs. Permissions are earned, not assumed — start with read-only, graduate to low-risk writes, then to transactions with approvals.

Stage-gate scope based on data: defect rate under X%, time-to-resolution under Y, and clean audit logs for Z weeks before you add a new permission.

Fallbacks matter more than prompts. Every action path needs a timeout, a rollback, and an escalation rule. If the agent can’t explain what it did, it didn’t happen.

How are you redesigning roles, controls, and metrics before you give agents the keys? #AIStrategy #AIAdoption #EnterpriseAI #DigitalTransformation
xPost: Scale agents like employees with badges: start read-only, earn permissions via SLOs, log everything, and require fallbacks. Intelligence isn’t the risk; uncontrolled work is. #AIStrategy #EnterpriseAI
